scope: Update numerical references at the chosen project endpoint; also record cumulative drift since their previous generation.
previous_reference_commit_description:
Refreeze after the growth factor on the dense z grid

generate_frozen_reference.py --overwrite, then --baryons, on cosmolike_core
a880d36 (Vivian's go-ahead, 2026-09-30). The frozen state now carries:
- the growth factor on the dense 1D z grid (the likelihood change of this
  repository's previous growth commit), which moved the references by
  <= 5.5e-4 in chi2 across the projects;
- the likelihood yaml keys added since the last freeze (include_HOD_GX,
  the halo-model IA key) in the expanded frozen configurations;
- the core fixes since then (lensing efficiencies on the shifted n(z)
  support, the HOD a grid) and the small drift of the old code against
  the previous references, which is no longer visible in the tests (it
  stays recoverable from this history).

The data folder equals the previous frozen copy; no data file changed.

Checked after the refreeze: test_example2.py (4 passed). The
full suite was NOT re-run after this refreeze.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
source_identity_note: The feature commit identifies the endpoint implementation. The binary hash identifies the exact executable used in these tests; later unrelated source commits are not a claim of a newer compiled binary.
interpretation: The endpoint comparisons hold the binary, physical parameters and all other numerical controls fixed. Their cosmic shear and individually Limber blocks must be identical. Changes in those blocks in the separate old-reference comparison cannot be attributed to the endpoint. That comparison spans the older source history and any deliberately updated numerical settings.
attribution_limit: This record measures each changed observable block. It does not assign cumulative historical differences to individual commits without an independent comparison.
